name: Ribbon app
desc: A ribbon driven entirely by rules: every button is one line on the Logic tab, narrowed to the command it answers (rib Command:bold), and the shape, the style, the density and the contextual tab are all rule verbs. What the window says about itself is worked out from the values rather than set by hand. Not one line of code.
vars:
doc = ""
mode = "office"
style = "fluent"
density = "comfortable"
picture = false
bold = false
italic = false
under = false
letters <- StrLen(doc)
look <- style " " density
said <- (picture ? "A picture is selected -- the Picture tab is showing" : letters ? letters " character" (letters = 1 ? "" : "s") : "Nothing typed yet")
styled <- (bold ? "bold " : "") (italic ? "italic " : "") (under ? "underlined" : "")

windows.name: Main
windows.title: Ribbon app
windows.status:
msg | Press Alt for the key tips | grow icon=E7C4
mode |  | right dim
windows.flows:
; --- the ribbon's own shape. One button, one line.
rib Command:m_office -> ribmode rib office
rib Command:m_office -> assign mode office
rib Command:m_simple -> ribmode rib simple
rib Command:m_simple -> assign mode simple
rib Command:m_strip -> ribmode rib strip
rib Command:m_strip -> assign mode strip
rib Command:m_titlebar -> ribmode rib titlebar
rib Command:m_titlebar -> assign mode titlebar
; --- how it looks
rib Command:s_fluent -> ribstyle rib fluent
rib Command:s_fluent -> assign style fluent
rib Command:s_classic -> ribstyle rib classic
rib Command:s_classic -> assign style classic
rib Command:s_flat -> ribstyle rib flat
rib Command:s_flat -> assign style flat
rib Command:s_outlined -> ribstyle rib outlined
rib Command:s_outlined -> assign style outlined
rib Command:d_compact -> ribdensity rib compact
rib Command:d_compact -> assign density compact
rib Command:d_comfortable -> ribdensity rib comfortable
rib Command:d_comfortable -> assign density comfortable
rib Command:d_roomy -> ribdensity rib roomy
rib Command:d_roomy -> assign density roomy
; --- the contextual tab: declared with the rest, shown when it applies
rib Command:picture -> ribshowtab rib pictools
rib Command:picture -> assign picture true
rib Command:picture -> ribtab rib pictools
rib Command:deselect -> ribhidetab rib pictools
rib Command:deselect -> assign picture false
; --- the three that stay in or out. `on` is which way it went.
rib Toggle:bold -> assign bold =on
rib Toggle:italic -> assign italic =on
rib Toggle:under -> assign under =on
; --- the rest
rib Command:file -> alert A backstage view would open here: New, Open, Save as.
rib Command:cut -> do docBox.Text := "", AxBindSync()
rib Command:paste -> do docBox.Text := docBox.Text A_Clipboard, AxBindSync()
rib Command:copy -> do A_Clipboard := docBox.Text
rib Command:copy -> toast Copied
rib Launcher:font -> alert The little arrow in a group's corner: a full Font dialog would open here.
rib TabPicked -> status msg ="On the " tabId " tab"
rib Collapse -> status msg =(rolledUp ? "Rolled up -- double-click a tab to bring it back" : "Rolled back down")
; --- the key tips, from the button as well as from Alt
rib Command:keytips -> ribkeytips rib
dropBtn Click -> ribhidetab rib pictools
dropBtn Click -> assign picture false
windows.binds:
docBox <-> doc
sumLabel.Text <- said
styleLabel.Text <- styled
dropBtn.Enabled <- picture
; the status bar's right-hand cell follows the shape it is in

kids.name: tip
kids.arg: Every button on this ribbon is one line on the Logic tab -- rib Command:bold -> ... -- because a ribbon raises one event for all of them and the studio can narrow it to each. Nothing here is written by hand: the shape, the style, the contextual tab and the three that stay in or out are all rules, and what the window says about itself is worked out from the values.

props.title: Forty buttons, forty rules, no code.

kids.name: docBox
kids.arg: A ribbon app: the ribbon above is the command surface, and this is the document.\n\nDouble-click a tab to roll the ribbon up, then click one to float it. Press Alt for the key tips. Insert > Picture brings up a contextual tab. View changes the ribbon's shape, style and density.
